In response to PoA comments:
Thank you for the careful review.
We would like to address the Cardano scope concern directly: 
(A) Midnight is using Cardano. Midnight is a Cardano partner chain part of the Cardano ecosystem, not a separate one. It is built on Input-Output's Partner Chains framework, Cardano SPOs can become Midnight validators, and specifically Midnight's 100% of its tokens [NIGHT] are only live and useful in Cardano as a native token.
(B) The template swaps to Cardano with a config change. EffectStream is multi-chain by design: the chain a template targets is a configuration + contract-package setting, not an app-logic rewrite. The same framework already runs templates natively on Cardano L1 today - stake-pool delegation, NFT pre-orders, and projected NFTs (cited below) - so pointing this template's stack at Cardano is a config update, not new work. The zero-knowledge commit-reveal that makes Kachina novel is written in Compact, and since Cardano L1 has no native ZK, that piece runs on Midnight - which is Cardano's ZK layer.
 (C) We have addressed this Catalyst Direction so that we can all be aligned on the focus, and how we are contributing to the Caradano Community and how this aligns with the proposal. The live demo uses Midnight in the live environment due to the cost of maintaing the servers, but native Cardano Tokens are now paying for users playing, making use of Cardano as the economic engine of the game. Please take a look at the additional notes for the official documentation.
We have update the information and created a video on youtube.

Deliverable: Kachina Kolosseum, the second game template - a novel multiplayer PvP game. On a public chain the second player can normally see the first player's move and counter it; Kachina's commit-reveal scheme removes that edge. ms.report:
NOTE: Due to short timelines for this project, we have submitted this milestone before the previous was approved. This was discussed with the Cardano Directive, and a formal statement was added at the end of the PoA. This milestone is totally independent from previous ones.
BRIEF
These templates are built to extend the Cardano ecosystem. Standard Cardano wallets. connect with a minor configuration change, because EffectStream targets the chain at the config level, not the app logic. Midnight, where these ZK templates run, is a Cardano partner chain: Cardano SPOs can become its validators, Midnight's NIGHT token lives on Cardano as a native token, and native Cardano tokens pay for the free-to-play demos. 
Dust-2-Dust, the fourth game template - the most technically complex of the set, a full roguelike deck builder written entirely in Compact. It is a complete game, not a proof of concept: hidden inventory, private resource management, and decisions that stay secret until their effects show up in play. Multiple interacting ZK circuits - drawing cards, using items, combat resolution, level progression - compose together, carrying hidden state across dozens of turns while preserving privacy throughout. All proofs run in the browser with WASM. Since Cardano L1 has no native ZK, the multi-circuit logic runs on Midnight - Cardano's ZK partner chain - and the pattern generalises to any game whose decisions depend on hidden state: deck builders, dungeon crawlers, stealth and strategy.

ms.report:
NOTE: Due to short timelines for this project, we have submitted this milestone before the previous was approved. This was discussed with the Cardano Directive, and a formal statement was added at the end of the PoA. This milestone is totally independent from previous ones.
BRIEF
These templates are built to extend the Cardano ecosystem. Standard Cardano wallets. connect with a minor configuration change, because EffectStream targets the chain at the config level, not the app logic. Midnight, where these ZK templates run, is a Cardano partner chain: Cardano SPOs can become its validators, Midnight's NIGHT token lives on Cardano as a native token, and native Cardano tokens pay for the free-to-play demos.
Go Fish, the fifth game template - a ZK implementation of "Mental Poker", the classic cryptographic problem of playing a fair card game with no trusted dealer. The protocol combines a commit-reveal scheme with shared secret derivation: the deck is encrypted so neither player can read it alone, and each card reveal requires cooperative decryption where both players contribute their share. Neither side can peek ahead or manipulate the draw order - a fair deal is enforced by the math, not by trust. Since Cardano L1 has no native ZK, the protocol runs on Midnight Cardano's ZK partner chain. Built on a single ZK contract, it implements any card-like game (poker, blackjack, trick-taking) trustlessly, and serves as a base layer any future card game on EffectStream can fork.
